stemBlocks.value: A binary operation o is defined by a o b = a² + b. Evaluate 2 o (3 o 4).
Think first: The bracket is an instruction to work out the inner operation first and feed its answer into the outer one.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p058-q11 from workbook page 58.

solutionSteps.instruction: Apply the rule again with a = 2, b = 13.

strategyBlocks.value: Evaluate 3 o 4 first, then use that result as the right-hand input of 2 o (...).

whyThisWorks.value: Brackets have the same priority with a binary operation as they do in ordinary arithmetic: the inner value must exist before the outer operation can use it. Because this operation is not associative, working left to right instead would give a different and wrong answer, so the bracket genuinely matters.

commonErrors.misconception: Working left to right and evaluating 2 o 3 first.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Working left to right and evaluating 2 o 3 first.

commonErrors.misconception: Squaring 13 instead of 2 in the final step.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Squaring 13 instead of 2 in the final step.

examTip.value: In nested binary operations, write the value of the bracket down as its own line before continuing.
